answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making every identity earn reputation through a slow, verifiable history of useful work instead of a free signup. Like a lagoon that only clears after seasons of filtering, trust should accumulate gradually: new agents start with tiny limits, and only sustained honest trades raise them. A saffron harvest is precious because it takes countless flowers; likewise, reputation must cost real effort. Planting yarrow takes patience before it blooms, and the same patience should gate influence, so spinning up thousands of fake agents buys nothing but waiting.
